description: Turn an itinerary into one navigable multi-stop route. Provide a `start` and `stops` (each a `location` {lat, lon} or a free-text `name` to geocode, plus optional `dwell_minutes` time at the stop), optional `depart_at` (RFC 3339) for absolute ETAs, `optimise: true` to reorder stops for the shortest day (VROOM solver), and `return_to_start`. Costing "auto", "truck" (with a `truck` profile the whole day respects dimensional/ADR restrictions), "bicycle", "pedestrian" or "motor_scooter". Returns the stops in visit order with per-leg duration/distance and arrival/departure times, totals, and the full route geometry (polyline6). Geocoded names carry a `resolution` — when `ambiguous` is true, check `alternatives` and re-run with an explicit location rather than trusting the guess.

CostingKind.description:
Costing models exposed by the MCP tools (a deliberate subset of the
Valhalla costing list), serialised in snake_case exactly as Valhalla
names them.

oneOf.description:
Truck costing; honours dimensional limits and, when a `truck`
profile is supplied, ADR dangerous-goods restrictions.
Bicycle costing; tune it with a `bicycle` options object.

Pedestrian (walking) costing; tune it with a `pedestrian` options
object (lit streets, wheelchair/blind, hiking difficulty).

Motor scooter (moped) costing: like auto but prefers lower-speed
roads and may use ways closed to larger motor vehicles.

LatLon.description: A WGS84 coordinate in decimal degrees: a {lat, lon} object (preferred), or a GeoJSON [lon, lat] array with LONGITUDE FIRST, the same order as every polygon field on this server.

PlanDayStopInput.description:
One stop of a `plan_day` itinerary: an exact location, or a free-text
name to geocode (ambiguous matches are flagged in the response, never
guessed silently).

dwell_minutes.description:
Time spent at the stop in minutes (default 0); shifts every later
ETA.

name.description: Free-text name or address, geocoded when no `location` is given.

TruckSpec.description:
Truck profile for routing: physical dimensions plus the ADR
dangerous-goods declaration. Omitted dimensions default to the EU
maximum authorised dimensions of Council Directive 96/53/EC (4.0 m
height, 2.55 m width, 16.5 m length, 40 t gross weight).

gross_weight_t.description: Gross combination weight in metric tonnes.

hazmat.description:
Whether the vehicle carries dangerous goods (ADR). Defaults to
false.

tunnel_code.description:
ADR 8.6.4 tunnel restriction code of the load, e.g. "B", "C5000D",
"B/D", or "(—)"/"none" for explicitly unrestricted. Leave unset if
unknown: a hazmat load without a code is conservatively treated as
code B (allowed only through category-A tunnels).

depart_at.description:
Departure time as RFC 3339 (e.g. "2026-07-18T09:00:00Z"); when
given, every ETA is also returned as an absolute timestamp.

optimise.description:
Reorder the stops for the shortest day (VROOM solver; requires the
optimisation sidecar). Default false: visit in the given order.

return_to_start.description: End the day back at the start (default false).

start.description: Where the day starts (name or location; `dwell_minutes` ignored).

stops.description:
The stops to visit (1–20). Visited in the given order unless
`optimise` is true.

truck.description:
Truck profile (dimensions + ADR declaration). Requires costing
"truck".

name: plan_day

label.description: Human-readable one-line label assembled from the address parts.

match.description:
How far this hit can be trusted to be the place that was asked
for — see [`GeocodeMatch`]. Present whenever the MapMap gateway
answered; absent on a deployment falling back to the direct Photon
geocoder, and absent on the gateway's own fast paths (a pasted
coordinate pair, a bare UK outward code, a category browse), which
answer without a ranking to report on.

name.description: Place name, when the source feature has one.

type.description:
Feature type, e.g. "house", "street", "city" (falls back to the
OSM value when the endpoint does not classify).

GeocodeMatch.description:
How well one geocoding result answers what was actually asked.

Geocoding's real failure mode is not "no answer" but a confident answer
to a different question: a plausible row on the wrong street, with
nothing in the response to say so. This object is that missing say-so,
and an agent should read it before acting on an address.

How to read it:

* Any component `unmatched` or `inferred` on the TOP hit means the
  answer does not carry the address that was asked for — an `unmatched`
  postcode means the result has no postcode at all, `inferred` means it
  has a different one. Neither is a match. Say so rather than presenting
  the hit as the address, and reach for `verify_places` when the address
  came from a model or a user and needs checking rather than using.
* A small `score_gap` means the ranking barely chose between this hit
  and the runner-up, which is exactly when to show the alternatives
  instead of picking one for the user.

components.description:
Per-component verdict on this hit: one entry for each structured
component supplied, and empty when the query was free text only.

score_gap.description:
The top result's score minus the runner-up's, rounded to 3 decimal
places. `0` for a single result, and `0` from the `photon` source,
which publishes no per-result score — so a `0` is "no signal", not
"a tie".

source.description:
Which backend answered: "mapmap-index" (the first-party index) or
"photon".

GeocodeMatchComponents.description:
Per-component verdicts inside a [`GeocodeMatch`]. Each is one of
"matched", "inferred" or "unmatched"; a component that was not supplied
is absent entirely.

* "matched" — the result's own field carries the value asked for (case-
  and accent-insensitive, and by containment, so `city: "London"`
  matches "City of London").
* "inferred" — the result carries a value for that component, but not
  the one asked for. It reached the page through ranking, as when a
  street is found by its transliterated name and displayed under its
  canonical one.
* "unmatched" — the result carries no value for that component at all.

LatLon.description: A WGS84 coordinate in decimal degrees: a {lat, lon} object (preferred), or a GeoJSON [lon, lat] array with LONGITUDE FIRST, the same order as every polygon field on this server.

PlanStart.description: The day's starting point as resolved.

name.description: The start's name, when one was given.

resolution.description: Geocoding details when the start was given as a name.

PlannedStop.description: One planned stop with its leg and ETAs.

arrival_at.description: Absolute arrival time (RFC 3339), when `depart_at` was given.

arrival_offset_s.description: Arrival, as seconds after departure from the start.

departure_at.description: Absolute departure time (RFC 3339), when `depart_at` was given.

departure_offset_s.description: Departure (arrival + dwell), as seconds after the day's start.

dwell_minutes.description: Dwell time applied at this stop, minutes.

input_index.description:
Index of this stop in the request's `stops` array (visit order may
differ when optimised).

name.description: The stop's name (from the request or the geocoder).

resolution.description: Geocoding details when the stop was given as a name.

travel_distance_m.description: Distance of the leg arriving at this stop, metres.

travel_duration_s.description: Travel time of the leg arriving at this stop, seconds.

ReturnLeg.description: The return leg of a `return_to_start` plan.

arrival_at.description: Absolute arrival time (RFC 3339), when `depart_at` was given.

arrival_offset_s.description: Arrival back at the start, seconds after departure.

travel_distance_m.description: Distance back to the start, metres.

travel_duration_s.description: Travel time back to the start, seconds.

StopResolution.description: How a free-text stop name was resolved to coordinates.

alternatives.description: Up to three alternative matches, best first.

ambiguous.description:
True when other plausible matches exist somewhere else — check
`alternatives` and re-run with an explicit `location` if the
chosen one is wrong.

costing.description: The costing the plan was routed with.

depart_at.description: The departure time echoed back, when one was given.

finish_at.description: Absolute end of the day (RFC 3339), when `depart_at` was given.

finish_offset_s.description: End of the day (last arrival + dwell), seconds after departure.

geometry_polyline6.description:
Full multi-stop route geometry (polyline6) — hand it to the map SDK
or the `route` tool consumers directly.

optimised.description: Whether the stop order was optimised (VROOM) or kept as given.

return_leg.description: The leg back to the start, when `return_to_start` was set.

stops.description:
The stops in visit order, each with leg, ETAs and any geocoding
resolution to double-check.

summary.description: One-line human-readable summary of the day.
